history.summary: CSV town corrected from 'Cheliama' to 'Cheliyama' (the standard village spelling). The Radha Vinod Temple at Cheliyama, Raghunathpur II block, is a Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Radha and Krishna, dated by its foundation inscription to 1619 Shakabda (1698 CE). Built in the atchala style (a variant of the char-chala form), it is a monument of national importance under the Archaeological Survey of India, noted for elaborate terracotta ornamentation on the facade, walls and columns depicting Krishnalila, Ramayana scenes (including the Rama-Ravana battle with war chariots), Vishnu's avatars, hunting episodes, royal processions and floral motifs. It stands on the southern bank of the Damodar river, ~1 km from the 11th-century rekha deul at Banda. Caution: some travel writing reports that unscientific modern restoration replaced many original terracotta panels with inferior new work. Coordinates are village/street-level from the map geocoder (Cheliama Road, Raghunathpur), not an exact temple POI, so they are approximate.

name: Radha Vinod Temple
town_description: Cheliyama (Cheliama) is a village in the Raghunathpur II block of Purulia district, the headquarters of its community development block, on State Highway 8 between Santaldih and Majhdia and on the southern bank of the Damodar river. It is known for its terracotta temples and proximity to the Banda Deul; it has basic schools and a rural hospital but little tourist infrastructure.
